title.narrative: International Assistance for the development of World Heritage Nominations in Africa, and SIDS

description.narrative: At its 41st Session of the UNESCO General Conference in November 2021, UNESCO Members States adopted Global Priority Africa 2022-2029, which includes five flagship Programmes. The Flagship Programme 3: Fostering Cultural Heritage and Capacity Development intends to tackle many challenges regarding World Heritage in Africa, including the issues of representativity and capacity development in Africa. In addition, UNESCO developed the Operational Strategy for Small Island Developing States (SIDS) (2023-2029) adopted in 2023. For that, at its decision 46 COM 14 the World Heritage Committee “call upon Member State to provide support to the SIDS in the implementation of the Strategy, by assisting Small Island Developing States non represented and under-represented in the preparation of their tentative lists and nomination files..” . With its partners, UNESCO seeks to tackle these representativity challenges through this initiative to empower experts, professionals, and stakeholders in developing solid nomination dossiers. The United States pledges 250,000 USD to support preparatory assistance for safeguarding World Heritage in Africa and SIDS through training programmes for the preparation of Tentative List and nomination dossiers.
